vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should require RUN_STARTED as the first event
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#the-run: a stream MUST begin with RUN_STARTED or RUN_ERROR; a consumer MUST treat anything else first as a protocol violation
vectors.notes: TS also asserts the error is an AGUIError instance (class name is TS-only).

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should not allow multiple RUN_STARTED events

expect.error: Cannot send 'RUN_STARTED' while a run is still active

vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#several-runs-on-one-stream: a RUN_STARTED while a run is still active is a violation
vectors.notes: Both RUN_STARTED events carry the same threadId/runId; the second is rejected regardless. Delivered-before-error counts asserted by the TS test are not part of an error vector.

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should not allow events after RUN_FINISHED (except RUN_ERROR)

expect.error: Cannot send event type 'TEXT_MESSAGE_START': The run has already finished with 'RUN_FINISHED'

vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#after-a-run-closes: a consumer MUST reject any event after RUN_FINISHED other than RUN_STARTED or a late RUN_ERROR
vectors.notes: RUN_FINISHED carries threadId/runId 'test' while RUN_STARTED carried 'test-thread-id'/'test-run-id', as in the TS test; TS verification does not match the two. Delivered-before-error counts asserted by the TS test are not part of an error vector. Input normalized: the TS test closes the run with a RUN_FINISHED whose threadId/runId differ from its RUN_STARTED (incidental); here they match, so the vector pins neither acceptance nor rejection of mismatched ids.

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should allow RUN_ERROR after RUN_FINISHED
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#after-a-run-closes: a producer MAY emit RUN_ERROR after RUN_FINISHED
vectors.notes: TS asserts 5 delivered events, the last RUN_ERROR. RUN_FINISHED ids differ from RUN_STARTED's, as in the TS test. Input normalized: the TS test closes the run with a RUN_FINISHED whose threadId/runId differ from its RUN_STARTED (incidental); here they match, so the vector pins neither acceptance nor rejection of mismatched ids.

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should allow RUN_ERROR at any time (even as first event)
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#the-run: a stream MAY begin with RUN_ERROR (a run can fail before it begins)
vectors.notes: TS asserts exactly one delivered event, RUN_ERROR.

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should not allow any events after RUN_ERROR

expect.error: Cannot send event type 'TEXT_MESSAGE_START': The run has already errored with 'RUN_ERROR'. No further events can be sent.

vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/events/lifecycle#after-a-run-closes: a producer MUST NOT emit anything after RUN_ERROR except RUN_STARTED; a consumer MUST reject it
vectors.notes: Delivered-before-error counts asserted by the TS test are not part of an error vector.

vectors.name: verifyEvents lifecycle > should allow a valid sequence of events
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/basic/patterns/streaming#open-content-close: open, content, close matched by identifier
vectors.notes: TS asserts 8 delivered events, first RUN_STARTED and last RUN_FINISHED. TEXT_MESSAGE_START carries no role; the explicit event is delivered without one (the assistant default is not materialised on explicit starts). Input normalized: the TS test closes the run with a RUN_FINISHED whose threadId/runId differ from its RUN_STARTED (incidental); here they match, so the vector pins neither acceptance nor rejection of mismatched ids.
